cases.name: down_m64_n64_k64_split4_w4_s3
must_audit: Native binder signature, constexpr, alignment/divisibility attributes and complete parsed NVIDIA options must match frozen expectations before exactly one build; source values are not a claimed native key.
Exactly one K loop and no persistent outer loop or speculative next-tile shared overwrite.

All 38 steps per split: last valid K tiles are 2368, 4800, 7232, 9664. Source has no masks because all real source elements are in bounds; compiler pipeline prefetches beyond each interval must be correctly predicated or absent.
Async copy waits/barriers protect current operands; outstanding WGMMA may not overlap a write to its shared stage, including every tail/zero-fill operation.
Final WGMMA and async-copy drains precede shared reuse, output-store staging, shared deallocation and kernel return. QKV's 40-step proof does not establish this 38-step specialization.
Each of 655360 FP32 partial values stored exactly once at (split*64+row)*2560+column; no BF16 partial conversion, atomics or residual/normalization path.
Record registers, shared bytes, stack/spill bytes, actual matrix instruction shape and all diagnostics. Reject spills, unproven stage ordering/bounds or unexpected launch semantics before runtime.

cases.name: sum_mn163840_split4_block1024

must_audit: Verify actual native inferred/default options, binder signature and divisibility attributes; explicit launch options alone do not establish the native specialization.
Four FP32 plane loads and sequential FP32 addition from zero, one BF16 result conversion; 163840 unique BF16 output elements.
Same-stream producer completion orders all partial stores before merge reads, and merge output precedes unchanged next normalization.

runtime_limitations: No device code was compiled or executed during preparation. CPU stand-ins do not establish BF16 model correctness, pipeline safety, occupancy or speed. No new full-verifier self-check or cache restoration machinery was added; only an official GPU run can establish complete verifier correctness.
